system_thesis: Extend the IEEE VIS 2026 identity through Swiss/International Typographic Style: a modular grid system, bold geometric forms, and high-contrast dark palette that scales from A2 poster to social media to conference badge. The visual language combines minimalist geometric composition with data visualization aesthetics — honoring the conference's academic rigor while projecting innovation and forward momentum.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary dark background for all deliverables. Near-black with subtle blue undertone.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Secondary panels, cards, elevated surfaces. Slightly lighter than ink for depth.

tokens.name: primary
tokens.usage: Primary accent color. Bright cyan/teal for key elements, CTAs, geometric highlights.

tokens.name: accent-warm
tokens.usage: Warm accent for secondary highlights, data visualization elements, contrast moments.

tokens.name: accent-cool
tokens.usage: Cool secondary accent. Indigo/violet for tertiary elements, gradients, depth.

tokens.name: text-primary
tokens.usage: Primary text on dark backgrounds. Pure white for maximum readability.

tokens.name: text-secondary
tokens.usage: Secondary text, captions, metadata. Light gray with cool undertone.

tokens.name: grid-line
tokens.usage: Subtle grid lines, dividers, structural elements. Visible but not dominant.

palette.strategy: Dark-mode-first palette anchored by near-black backgrounds with bright accent colors. High contrast for readability and visual impact. Accent colors reference data visualization palettes while maintaining brand distinction. The palette must remain consistent across all deliverables — no format introduces new colors outside this system.

display.usage: Oversized headlines, conference name, key messages. Geometric, modern, commanding presence.
display.notes: Use tight tracking for impact. Can be set very large (72pt+ on poster). All caps acceptable for short headlines.

headline.usage: Section headers, dates, location. Secondary emphasis below display.
headline.notes: Slightly lighter than display but still bold. Maintains geometric character.

body.usage: Body text, descriptions, research areas, registration info.
body.notes: Clean, highly readable sans-serif. Neutral, lets content breathe.

caption.notes: Smaller size, text-secondary color. Maintains readability at small sizes.

data.usage: Data-like elements, technical labels, coordinates, grid references.
data.notes: Monospace for technical/data aesthetic. Use sparingly for accent, not body text.

typography.scale: Modular type scale based on 1.25 ratio. Poster display: 120-180pt. Poster headline: 48-72pt. Poster body: 18-24pt. Social display: 48-72pt. Social body: 14-18pt. Badge display: 24-36pt. Badge body: 10-12pt.
typography.strategy: Two-typeface system: Space Grotesk for expressive headlines (geometric, modern, distinctive) and Inter for readable body text (neutral, functional). JetBrains Mono as technical accent. All sans-serif, maintaining clean academic tone while allowing bold expression in headlines.

grid.social: Adapted 6-column grid for square formats, 4-column for stories. Maintains 8px base unit.
grid.badge: 4-column grid, 4px gutter, 8px margin. Compact but legible.
grid.notes: All deliverables align to the 8px base unit. Grid ensures visual consistency across formats. Elements should snap to grid lines. Whitespace is intentional, not accidental.

motif_system.name: Geometric Data Forms
motif_system.description: Original geometric patterns inspired by data visualization and hexagonal structures. NOT a copy of the website hex-pattern, but an evolution of the aesthetic into bold, abstract geometric compositions.
elements: Abstract hexagonal clusters (simplified, geometric, not literal hex pattern)
Network node diagrams (circles connected by lines, suggesting data flow)
Geometric color blocks (rectangles, triangles, circles in accent colors)
Grid intersections (points where grid lines meet, emphasized with dots or small shapes)
Data visualization abstractions (bar charts, scatter plots, flow diagrams as decorative elements)
rules: Geometric forms must be abstract, not literal representations
Use accent colors (primary, accent-warm, accent-cool) for geometric elements
Forms should suggest data/visualization without being specific charts
Maintain clean edges, no gradients or soft shadows on geometric elements
Geometric elements support the message hierarchy, never overwhelm it

do_say: IEEE VIS 2026 — The Premier Forum for Visualization
Advances in Theory, Methods, and Applications
do_not_say: The future of data is here

lockup.primary: IEEE master logo (top-left) + IEEE VIS 2026 logo (center or prominent) + IEEE VGTC logo (bottom-right or footer)
rules: IEEE master logo must appear on all deliverables per IEEE brand guidelines
IEEE VIS 2026 logo is the primary conference mark, set prominently
IEEE VGTC logo appears as co-organizer, smaller than VIS logo
Logos must not be recreated, modified, or recolored — use official files only
On dark backgrounds: use white versions of all logos
Minimum clear space: 1x logo height around each logo
Logo order: IEEE (master brand) → VIS 2026 (conference) → VGTC (co-organizer)
lockup.poster_lockup: IEEE logo top-left, VIS 2026 logo centered or upper-third, VGTC logo bottom-right with dates/location
lockup.social_lockup: IEEE logo top-left corner, VIS 2026 logo prominent, VGTC logo bottom or footer
lockup.badge_lockup: IEEE logo top, VIS 2026 logo center, VGTC logo bottom. Compact arrangement.
lockup.ppt_lockup: IEEE logo top-left corner of all slides, VIS 2026 logo on title slide only, VGTC logo on title slide footer

imagery_strategy.approach: Abstract geometric composition with data visualization aesthetics. No stock photography. No literal data visualizations. Geometric forms suggest the field without illustrating it directly.
imagery_strategy.boston_context: Optional subtle Boston skyline silhouette or reference, but not dominant. The conference is in Boston, but the visual identity should be universal and academic, not tourist-focused.
imagery_strategy.people: No people in the visual system. Focus on abstract geometric forms and typography.
imagery_strategy.texture: Subtle texture allowed (paper grain, noise) but keep it minimal. The aesthetic is clean and digital-first.

consistency_lock.description: The main poster establishes the visual system: dark background, bold geometric composition, oversized Space Grotesk typography, bright accent colors, and logo lockup. All other deliverables adapt this same visual idea to their format.
must_preserve: Bold geometric forms in accent colors
High contrast between text and background
Logo lockup order and placement logic
adaptation_rules: Social media formats crop or rearrange the geometric composition but maintain the same color palette and typography
Badge scales down the visual system, prioritizing logo and essential info
PPT template uses the same palette and typography, with geometric elements as slide backgrounds or accents
All formats maintain the dark-mode aesthetic and high contrast

do_not_use: Generic AI-generated conference poster clichés (gradient blobs, abstract tech circles, glowing nodes)
Stock photography of people or offices
Literal data visualizations (actual charts, graphs, dashboards)
More than 3 accent colors in one composition
Recreating or modifying the official IEEE/VIS/VGTC logos
